lessons.title: Out of the Flow: Position, Z-index, Float and a Gallery

objectives.cognitive: Name the five position values and explain what float, clear and z-index do.
objectives.affective: Value pages where nothing important is covered or hidden.
objectives.psychomotor: Place a ribbon on Juan's projects header and float his first gallery pictures in CodeShare.

blocks.markdown: **How to use this module:** Work in order, Monday to Friday. Run every sample unchanged first, then do its small task. Answer each day's exit slip after its last step.

**Everything happens in CodeShare.** Open your class, then **Module**, this week and a step. **Work in code editor** loads the step's sample files into the editor tabs; **Run code** shows the step's run page in the page window and checks it, and its links open the project's other pages there. It works online and from the classroom laptop; no internet, installation, download or account is needed.

**Reading the outputs:** an output box shows the page text CodeShare checks for the step's run page: the Tab title, the Visible page text, then, on Steps 2, 4, 5, 6 and 9, Media checks. position, offsets, z-index and float are not page text; page checks read them. But a box taken out of the flow with position: absolute or float becomes a block, so its words get their own line. Captions are page text; alt is not. Spaces count.

**Where we start:** Juan's finished Week 6 site (three pages and styles.css) carries forward in your module project. Each step loads its run page and every file it needs; boxes show only new or changed lines.
**Week 7 starts here:** Juan's site is spaced and has a nav bar, but every box sits in the normal flow, one under another: nothing overlaps, nothing sits side by side.

blocks.term: Position, z-index, float and a gallery
blocks.markdown: position chooses how a box is placed: static (the normal flow), relative (moved from its own place), absolute (placed from its nearest positioned ancestor), fixed (from the window) or sticky (normal until you scroll, then held). top, right, bottom and left give the distances. z-index decides which positioned box is on top. float: left or right moves a box to one side so the next content wraps beside it; clear starts a box below the floats. A gallery is a set of figures, each an img with its figcaption.

A bulletin board: most papers are pinned in rows (the normal flow), a sticky note is stuck on top of one corner (absolute, with a higher z-index), and a photo pinned at the left lets the paper's words run beside it (float).

rows: in the normal flow; top and left do nothing
static; a top you set, with no effect
moved from its own place; its space stays
from the nearest positioned ancestor; its space closes
the sides you set in px
from the window; stays while you scroll
normal until you scroll, then held at top
no: it groups the picture and its caption
no: alt is read aloud by screen readers, not shown
no: every picture the same size

blocks.markdown: **Media steps:** Steps 2, 4, 5, 6 and 9 run index.html, with Juan's picture, sound, video and gallery pictures, files your teacher adds under Media files. Online, CodeShare checks them automatically; Run code waits on Loading media… until they are on this device. Offline, these five steps show Checked by your teacher for now, and your teacher presses Mark done. Steps 1, 3, 7 and 8 run projects.html and are checked automatically.

blocks.instruction: Juan's Week 6 site carries forward. position: absolute takes an element out of the page's flow and places it by top, right, bottom and left, measured from its nearest positioned ancestor. The h1 gets position: relative, so it becomes that ancestor; the new ribbon sits 8px from the h1's top-right corner, and z-index: 1 keeps it above the h1. Run projects.html unchanged.

blocks.markdown: **Practice: what does the page check read?** (a) z-index: 3 on a span with no position; (b) top: 8px on Juan's ribbon; (c) the ribbon's position when the ; after absolute is missing; (d) left on Juan's ribbon, which sets only top and right. Answers: (a) 3, but it does nothing; (b) 8px; (c) static; (d) a px value that changes with the window, so it is never checked.

**Values that follow the window:** a side you did not set (left on Juan's ribbon), anything fixed, and a sticky box's place while you scroll change with the window's size, and CodeShare's page window is not the same size on every screen. Page checks read only the sides you set in px; set picture sizes in px, never %.
Answer the Monday exit slip now.

questions.prompt: Name the five values of position.
In Step 1, the ribbon got position: absolute, and ICT STRAND moved to its own line in the output. Why?
In Week 6, display: inline-block put nav items on one line. In Step 2, float: left puts figures side by side. How are they alike?

lessons.title: Placing and Stacking: Sticky, Z-index and Text Wrap

objectives.cognitive: Explain how top, right, bottom and left place relative, absolute and sticky elements, and which z-index wins.
objectives.affective: Appreciate a layout that keeps the navigation reachable for every reader.
objectives.psychomotor: Keep Juan's nav on top with sticky and z-index, and wrap his introduction around his floated picture.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's ribbon and first gallery pictures are placed, but his nav scrolls away, and his picture sits alone above his introduction.

relative moves a box but keeps its old space; absolute removes the box from the flow, so the next content moves up. Page checks read top, right, bottom and left as you wrote them in px; a side you did not set reads a px value that follows the window. A higher z-index paints on top, but only on a positioned box: z-index on a static box reads its value and does nothing. A floated picture lets text wrap around it.
A jeepney's signboard stays at the top of the windshield while the road moves past (sticky), and a sticker on the glass is always in front of the board (a higher z-index).

rows: left: a px value, different on every screen
it follows the window: never check it
`top: 1em;` on a relative span in the 32px h1
read as written, but it does nothing

blocks.instruction: position: sticky keeps the nav in its place until you scroll, then holds it at top: 0. Juan's h1 is positioned too and comes later in the page, so without a z-index it would slide over the nav: z-index: 2 keeps the nav on top, and a white background hides what scrolls under it. float: right sends each badge to the right edge of its line. Run projects.html unchanged.

lessons.title: Pictures in a Row: An Image Gallery with Captions

objectives.cognitive: Describe how figure, img and figcaption build a gallery, and why captions are page text but alt is not.
objectives.affective: Respect the people and work shown in pictures by describing them honestly.
objectives.psychomotor: Build Juan's gallery with equal picture sizes, captions and a positioned tag.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's gallery pictures have different sizes and plain captions.

A gallery is a row of figures; each figure groups an img (src, alt, width, height) with its figcaption. Float the figures left with a px width and give every picture the same size in px. Captions are page text; alt is not, but screen readers read it.
A school yearbook page: pictures of the same size in a row, each with its caption underneath.

blocks.instruction: Every gallery picture gets the same size, 160px by 110px, and a thin grey border; each caption is centred in 13px text. The certificate joins the gallery. Run index.html unchanged.

performanceTask.title: My Resume, Week 7: A Picture Gallery and a Positioned Element
performanceTask.markdown:
Start Thursday; finish and present Friday. In CodeShare open Projects, then Personal performance-task project. Your Week 6 site carries forward: add this week's gallery to index.html and this week's rules to your own styles.css.

Add a gallery of three or more of your projects, certificates or activities on index.html, and one positioned element, such as a ribbon in your h1. Pictures are your own (only you or no people in them) or your teacher's. Online, add each under Media files in images, named with letters, numbers, - and _ only (my_poster.jpg), at most 5 MB and 10 files. Offline, Media files are not available yet: write the figures and captions now: Run code still succeeds, and each picture shows only its alt text and a small broken-picture icon until its file is added online.

Use only safe details: no home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or personal social-media accounts, and no other people in any picture. Run code until index.html runs with no error, then press Submit this version. Saving or running is not submitting.

Thursday: 0–60 minutes, repairs and the Thursday strip; 60–120 minutes, plan on paper, show the teacher, then start. Friday: 0–30 minutes, finish and run; 30–105 minutes, five-minute presentations; 105–120 minutes, Friday strip and Submit this version.
checklist: Keep your Week 6 site: every page, the nav bar and styles.css linked from every page.
On index.html, a gallery of three or more figures, each an img (src in images/, honest alt, width, height) and a figcaption.
Float the gallery's figures left with a width in px; give every picture the same size in px.
The heading or paragraph after the gallery has clear: both.
One positioned element: absolute inside a parent with position: relative, top and right (or left) in px, and a z-index.
Its text and background colours from the chart: 4.5:1 or more.
Nothing in url(); no address, phone, birth date, ID numbers, social media or other people in a picture.
Run code shows no error; online every picture shows; press Submit this version, then present.
